cards.name: Short strangle
cards.one_liner: Sell an out-of-the-money put and call in the same expiration; you are paid for implied volatility running above what the market realizes, and you carry undefined risk on both sides.

when.iv: IV rank above 50 is tastylive's 'sell' zone [page:concepts-implied-volatility-rank-percentile]. Our test found high IV rank no better on average and with a far worse tail [repro:vrp_spx].
when.outlook: Neutral: the underlying expected to stay between the short strikes [page:concepts-strangle].
when.events: Avoid holding through a known binary event unless that is the trade (see the earnings card).

avoid: Low implied volatility: thin premium with full exposure to a volatility spike; the worst losses came from strangles opened in calm markets right before a sudden IV jump [ep:market-measures-2025-08-14@06:44].
When a large move is expected [page:concepts-strangle].
IRA and cash accounts: naked strangles are not allowed [lit:tastytrade-ira-2026].
Illiquid underlyings with wide markets [page:concepts-options-liquidity].

setup.dte: About 45 days (30-60) [page:concepts-strangle] [ep:research-2023-10-20@00:02]; lengthen toward 60-65 days when IV is low [ep:market-measures-2024-06-17@00:17].
setup.strikes: About 16 delta on each side, roughly the 1-standard-deviation expected move [ep:market-measures-2023-02-22@03:07] [page:concepts-standard-deviation]; some hosts use about 20 delta [ep:options-jive-2024-01-16@07:42].
setup.credit_target: No fixed credit target for strangles on the pages reviewed; the credit follows from the deltas and IV.
setup.underlying: Liquid index products (SPY, SPX, /ES); the variance premium is larger and more reliable for indexes than single stocks [lit:carr-wu-2009].

manage.profit_target: Close at 50% of the credit received [page:concepts-strangle] [page:concepts-managing-winners].
manage.time_exit: Close or roll at about 21 DTE, whichever comes first with the profit target [ep:market-measures-2024-06-17@08:59] [ep:market-measures-2023-08-04@09:22].
manage.roll: Roll out in time only for a net credit, about 7-21 days before expiration [page:concepts-defending-positions].
manage.defend: When one side is tested, roll the untested side closer to the price to collect more credit and move the breakeven [page:concepts-strangle].
manage.loss_rule: tastylive: close at a net loss of 2x the credit received [page:concepts-defending-positions]. Our test: a 2x-credit stop lowered the mean slightly but cut the worst crash-period loss from -28.8 to -4.7 credits (March 2020, closes only) [repro:strangle_mgmt].

size.bpr_formula: Each naked leg (Reg T): premium + max(20% of underlying - OTM amount, 10% floor) x 100; 15% instead of 20% for broad indexes such as SPX/XSP [lit:finra-4210-2026]. Strangle total = larger leg's requirement + the other leg's premium (standard practice; source not yet verified). Portfolio margin uses stress tests instead [lit:tastytrade-pm-2026].
size.per_trade: Keep each trade under about 5% of the account so results come from many occurrences [page:concepts-number-of-occurrences].
size.notes: Use 25-50% of buying power across all positions, never above 75%: higher in high volatility and small accounts, lower in low volatility and large accounts [ep:options-jive-2023-12-27@06:56]. Size as equity risk: short index puts carry a beta of about 0.56-0.60 [lit:bondarenko-2019].

It is crash-exposed, and retail 16-delta strangles net of costs, margin and tails have no independent test (C). Overall B: real but sensitive to period and implementation. conventions.rule: Take profit at 50%
conventions.effect: Raises the win rate and P&L per day (more turnover), lowers P&L per trade; adds no expected edge by itself [repro:strangle_mgmt] [lit:williams-1991].

conventions.rule: Exit at 21 DTE
conventions.effect: Cuts the worst-5% loss (about a third in our model, roughly half in tastylive's SPY data) and gives up the remaining premium [repro:strangle_mgmt] [ep:market-measures-2023-08-04@04:13].

conventions.rule: Close at a 2x-credit loss
conventions.effect: Turns open-ended tails into realized losses and gives up recoveries: in our model it lowered the mean (+0.21 vs +0.26 credits) but cut the worst trade of March 2020 from -28.8 to -4.7 credits (closes only; real fills slip) [repro:strangle_mgmt] [lit:kaminski-lo-2014].

history.change: Managing winners at 50% of max profit studied and promoted as the default exit.
The 21-DTE exit becomes common guidance: it appears in 45 episode titles/tags in 2017-2021 against 2 in 2012-2016 (archive popularity count); later studies test it directly.
Guidance to lengthen duration toward 60-65 DTE when IV is low.

mistakes: Forgetting the call side has unlimited risk [page:concepts-strangle].
Treating a high win rate as safety: losing trades averaged little, but the worst was 27x the credit [ep:market-measures-2025-08-14@03:22].
Rolling for a debit, which worsens the breakeven while opening a low-probability trade [page:concepts-defending-positions].
Holding into the last weeks before expiration, where gamma and tail losses grow [ep:market-measures-2023-08-04@09:22].
Selling in low IV for thin premium [ep:market-measures-2025-08-14@06:44].

cards.name: Short straddle
cards.one_liner: Sell an at-the-money put and call at the same strike and expiration; you collect the most premium of any neutral structure, but the breakevens are narrow and the risk is undefined on both sides.

when.iv: tastylive: favor the short straddle when IV is high and stability is expected [page:concepts-straddle]; high IV rank favors short premium [page:concepts-mean-reversion-explained]. Our test found high IV rank no better for the average vol spread and a far worse tail [repro:vrp_spx].
when.outlook: Neutral: expects stability, with price staying near the strike [page:concepts-straddle].
when.events: Not covered on the straddle page. Earnings straddles are a separate trade (see the earnings card); late-day 0DTE straddles lost money in a tastylive study [ep:market-measures-2024-05-14@03:01].

avoid: Low implied volatility: the short straddle is listed as a high-IV structure [page:concepts-straddle].
When a large move is expected; a long straddle is the low-IV, big-move choice [page:concepts-straddle].
IRA and cash accounts: naked options are not allowed there [lit:tastytrade-ira-2026].
Selling 0DTE straddles in the last half hour: the 40% win rate and doubled tail loss lost money overall [ep:market-measures-2024-05-14@03:01].
Illiquid underlyings with wide markets [page:concepts-options-liquidity].

setup.dte: About 45 days, which tastylive research found balances shorter and longer durations [page:concepts-straddle].
setup.strikes: Both legs at the same, at-the-money strike (structure). Higher IV means more credit, wider breakevens and a higher chance of success [page:concepts-straddle]. No delta rule beyond that on the pages reviewed.
setup.credit_target: No fixed credit target for straddles on the pages reviewed; the credit follows from IV.
setup.underlying: Liquid index products; the variance premium is larger and more reliable for indexes than single stocks, where the level premium was significant for only 3 of 35 names [lit:carr-wu-2009].

manage.profit_target: No straddle-specific target on the pages reviewed. tastylive's general default is about 50% of max profit for most trades [page:concepts-managing-winners].
manage.time_exit: No straddle-specific time exit found. The 21-DTE evidence was gathered on SPY naked puts and strangles: largest losses down almost 50%, average losses down 60% [lit:tastylive-cutlosses-nd].
manage.roll: General premium-selling rule: roll out in time only for a net credit, about 7-21 days before expiration [page:concepts-defending-positions].
manage.defend: No straddle-specific defense on the pages reviewed. The general rule is to roll for a credit and not for a debit [page:concepts-defending-positions].
manage.loss_rule: tastylive: close at a net loss of 2x the credit received (general premium-selling rule) [page:concepts-defending-positions]. The literature finds a simple stop-loss has a negative expected effect without momentum [lit:kaminski-lo-2014]; no straddle-specific test of the 2x stop was found.

size.bpr_formula: Each naked leg (Reg T): premium + max(20% of underlying - OTM amount, 10% floor) x 100; 15% instead of 20% for broad indexes such as SPX/XSP [lit:finra-4210-2026]. At the money the OTM amount is zero, so each leg is premium + 20% of the underlying. Straddle total = larger leg's requirement + the other leg's premium (standard practice; not yet verified). Portfolio margin uses stress tests [lit:tastytrade-pm-2026].
size.per_trade: Keep each trade under about 5% of the account [page:concepts-number-of-occurrences].
size.notes: Use 25-50% of buying power across all positions, never above 75% [ep:options-jive-2023-12-27@06:56]. Size as equity risk: the short-premium book behaves like lower-beta equity exposure with negative skew (PUT beta about 0.56-0.60) [lit:bondarenko-2019]. The straddle has the most gamma of any neutral structure, so keep positions small (structure).

evidence.note: The edge is the index variance risk premium (replicated, A) [lit:coval-shumway-2001] [lit:bondarenko-2019], and ATM straddle returns are directly documented as negative for buyers, but Broadie et al. find ATM straddle returns harder to explain than OTM puts [lit:broadie-etal-2009]. The structure itself has only one tastylive approach page and a late-day 0DTE study, with no 45-DTE straddle study or repro of our own, so the card is C: the premium is real, a retail naked straddle after costs, margin and tails is untested.

conventions.rule: Close winners at about 50% of max profit (general default)
conventions.effect: Raises turnover and the win rate; adds no expected edge by itself, since exit rules cannot change a fair game's expectation [page:concepts-managing-winners] [lit:williams-1991].

conventions.rule: Close at a 2x-credit loss (general default)
conventions.effect: Turns open-ended tails into realized losses; negative stopping premium without momentum [page:concepts-defending-positions] [lit:kaminski-lo-2014].

Selling when IV is low and thin credit gives narrow breakevens [page:concepts-straddle].
Reading a high win rate as safety; the late-day study shows wins can still lose money overall [ep:market-measures-2024-05-14@03:01].
Rolling for a debit, which worsens the breakeven [page:concepts-defending-positions].

cards.name: Iron condor
cards.one_liner: A short strangle with long wings: sell an OTM put spread and an OTM call spread in one expiration, collect the credit and keep the loss capped at the wing width minus the credit.

when.iv: No IV-rank rule on tastylive's iron condor page. In high IV (VIX above 35) the wide condor still collects about 60% of the strangle's median P&L with about 33% less tail risk, and the two need about the same buying power [ep:market-measures-2023-02-22@05:45].
when.outlook: Neutral: price expected to stay between the short strikes (defined-risk short strangle) [page:concepts-iron-condor].
when.events: No guidance on the condor page. For earnings, tastylive's 16/10-delta condor study had returns on investment from about -9% to +9% [ep:research-2024-10-21@03:19].

avoid: Pushing the wings extremely far out: far strikes pay almost nothing and are illiquid; stay near 5-delta wings [ep:market-measures-2023-02-22@07:45].
Very short durations without small size: 7-DTE condors had about 49 max-loss trades vs 8 at 45 DTE over the test period [ep:research-2023-10-20@05:13].
Holding a tested short strike into expiration: close before it goes in the money to avoid assignment into shares [page:concepts-iron-condor].
Illiquid names, and names that rarely move on earnings [ep:research-2024-10-21@07:51].

setup.dte: Research continues to favor about 45 DTE as the best risk-return point for selling premium [ep:research-2023-10-20@00:02]. In the 25-delta test, win rate stayed in the mid-60s regardless of duration [ep:research-2023-10-20@05:13].
setup.strikes: Short strikes at about 16 delta with long wings at about 5 delta (a wide condor standing in for a strangle) [ep:market-measures-2023-02-22@03:07]. A 25-delta short, 5-delta wing version was also tested [ep:research-2023-10-20@05:13]. Prefer far-OTM strikes for the condor [page:concepts-iron-condor].
setup.credit_target: About one-third of the strike width [page:concepts-iron-condor].
setup.underlying: SPY and SPX in the studies reviewed [ep:market-measures-2023-02-22@03:07] [ep:market-measures-2026-09-25@04:08]; liquid chains.

manage.profit_target: Close at 50% of max profit [page:concepts-iron-condor].
manage.time_exit: No condor-specific time exit on the page. Managing a 45-DTE trade at 21 DTE leaves a smaller zone to survive, about 73% of the expiration distance (Black-Scholes) [ep:research-2025-03-12@05:55].
manage.roll: Roll only for a net credit, about 7-21 days before expiration [page:concepts-defending-positions].
manage.defend: Roll the untested side closer to the stock price to collect more premium; moving it to the tested strike forms an iron fly [page:concepts-iron-condor].
manage.loss_rule: General tastylive rule: close at a net loss of 2x the credit [page:concepts-defending-positions]. For 0DTE condors the hosts say size small enough to leave alone or stop at about 2x the credit [ep:market-measures-2026-09-25@03:25]; not tested on 45-DTE condors in the material reviewed.

size.bpr_formula: Defined risk: (wing width x 100) - credit received, per condor (only one side can lose). Example: $5 wings and $1.65 credit = $335.
size.per_trade: Keep each trade under about 5% of the account [page:concepts-number-of-occurrences].
size.notes: Use 25-50% of buying power across all positions, never above 75% [ep:options-jive-2023-12-27@06:56]. A $5-wide 5-delta-wing condor needs about 2.5x less buying power than the 16-delta strangle [ep:market-measures-2023-02-22@03:07]. IRA accounts allow defined-risk spreads [lit:tastytrade-ira-2026]. Cash-account eligibility of spreads is broker-specific and not sourced here.

evidence.note: The condor inherits the strangle's variance-risk-premium edge but the wings are insurance that consumes most of it: tastylive's own test shows the wide condor keeps about 60% of the median profit with 38% less tail [ep:market-measures-2023-02-22@03:07], and the Cboe condor index earned about cash or less since 2007 [repro:cboe_short_vol] [lit:moran-2021b]. Documented but period- and implementation-sensitive, so B; value is the capped loss and lower buying power, not extra return.

conventions.rule: Collect about one-third of the width
conventions.effect: Sets the entry probability of profit near 67% and the strike distance; a pricing rule, not a source of return [page:concepts-iron-condor].

conventions.rule: Take profit at 50% of max profit
conventions.effect: Raises win rate and turnover, lowers P&L per trade; adds no expected edge by itself [page:concepts-iron-condor] [lit:williams-1991].

conventions.rule: Roll the untested side closer
conventions.effect: Collects more credit and moves the breakeven, but adds exposure in the losing direction; a roll is a close plus a new trade [page:concepts-iron-condor] [lit:sec-ljm-2021].

conventions.rule: Close at a 2x-credit loss
conventions.effect: Turns tails into realized losses; negative stopping premium without momentum [page:concepts-defending-positions] [lit:kaminski-lo-2014].

mistakes: Treating the cap on loss as a cap on cost: the wings consume most of the premium (CNDR about 1% a year since 2007) [repro:cboe_short_vol].
Assuming a high win rate means a safe trade; at 7 DTE the 25-delta condor still had many max-loss trades [ep:research-2023-10-20@05:13].
Going to extremely wide wings for buying power; the far strikes pay almost nothing [ep:market-measures-2023-02-22@07:45].
Letting a short strike go in the money into expiry [page:concepts-iron-condor].

cards.name: Iron fly / iron butterfly
cards.one_liner: Sell an at-the-money straddle and buy out-of-the-money wings: the most credit of the neutral defined-risk structures, with a narrow profit zone and a capped loss.

when.iv: tastylive uses the iron fly with a neutral view in a high-IV stock; it profits when volatility contracts [page:concepts-iron-butterfly]. No IV-rank threshold on the page.
when.outlook: Neutral: price expected to finish near the short strike [page:concepts-iron-butterfly].
when.events: No event guidance on the pages reviewed.

avoid: A big expected move: the profit zone is narrow, with worse breakevens than a condor, and one leg is almost always in the money [page:concepts-iron-condor].
Letting price run to a wing: adjust or exit early to limit the loss [page:concepts-iron-butterfly].
Holding in-the-money short legs into expiry: close them before expiration to avoid assignment [page:concepts-iron-butterfly].

setup.dte: No tastylive guidance found in the reviewed pages; no DTE rule for the iron fly.
setup.strikes: Short put and short call at the same at-the-money strike, long wings above and below (structure). Wing width is not specified on the pages reviewed.
setup.credit_target: No tastylive guidance found in the reviewed pages; no credit target.
setup.underlying: A high-IV stock, per tastylive [page:concepts-iron-butterfly]; liquidity matters for four legs [page:concepts-options-liquidity].

manage.profit_target: Manage at a lower level than the 50% default: between 10% and 50% of max profit for iron flies [page:concepts-managing-winners].
manage.time_exit: No tastylive guidance found in the reviewed pages.
manage.roll: No fly-specific roll rule. General: roll only for a net credit, about 7-21 days before expiration [page:concepts-defending-positions].
manage.defend: If price moves toward a wing, adjust or exit early to limit the loss; close early to lock in a large share of max profit [page:concepts-iron-butterfly]. A condor can be rolled into a fly by moving the untested side to the tested strike [page:concepts-iron-condor].
manage.loss_rule: No fly-specific stop. General tastylive rule: close at a net loss of 2x the credit [page:concepts-defending-positions]; for a defined-risk fly check it against the max loss.

size.bpr_formula: Defined risk: (wing width x 100) - credit received, per fly (only one side can lose).
size.per_trade: Keep each trade under about 5% of the account [page:concepts-number-of-occurrences].
size.notes: Use 25-50% of buying power across all positions, never above 75% [ep:options-jive-2023-12-27@06:56]. IRA accounts allow defined-risk spreads [lit:tastytrade-ira-2026]. Cash-account eligibility of spreads is broker-specific and not sourced here.

cards.name: 0DTE structures
cards.one_liner: A horizon, not a single trade: options that expire the same session, usually run as short defined-risk condors or strangles near the open. Premium decays fastest here, but the premium is small next to spreads and the tail losses are large.

when.iv: No IV rule on the tastylive 0DTE pages reviewed. Small losses mostly came from volatility expansion; losses of 1x credit and beyond mostly came from strike breaches [ep:market-measures-2026-09-25@04:08].

avoid: Selling 0DTE premium with about half an hour left in the session: large tail losses outweigh small credits [ep:market-measures-2024-05-14@03:22].
Riding a late-day short position to expiration; close it with about 30 minutes left [ep:market-measures-2024-05-14@03:43].
Over-leveraging short 0DTE options, and illiquid strikes with wide spreads and slippage [page:concepts-how-to-trade-0dte-options].
Treating 0DTE as the efficient duration: tastylive research points to about 45 DTE for short options [page:concepts-zero-days-0dte-options-explained].

setup.strikes: Studied: 16-delta SPX iron condor with 10-wide wings opened near the open [ep:market-measures-2026-09-25@04:08]; strangles $10, $20 or $30 out sold at the open and closed after 90 minutes [ep:market-measures-2024-05-14@02:27].

manage.time_exit: Sell near the open and manage quickly: the morning approach closed after 90 minutes was workable [ep:market-measures-2024-05-14@04:03]. Close any short premium still open with about 30 minutes left [ep:market-measures-2024-05-14@03:43].
manage.roll: No tastylive guidance found in the reviewed pages; no roll guidance for 0DTE.
manage.defend: Treat a loss of about 1x the credit as the decision point for whether to close; recovery odds are about a coin flip there [ep:market-measures-2026-09-25@08:19].
manage.loss_rule: Size small enough to leave the trade alone when tested, or stop at about 2x the credit [ep:market-measures-2026-09-25@03:25]. Predefine the exit [page:concepts-how-to-trade-0dte-options].

The pattern day trader rule and $25,000 minimum were eliminated effective 4 Jun 2026 (brokers may phase in to 20 Oct 2027), replaced by intraday margin standards [lit:finra-rn26-10-2026]. cards.name: Earnings trade (vol crush)
cards.one_liner: Sell premium before a scheduled earnings report and buy it back after, aiming to keep the implied-volatility crush; the risk is the gap move, so size small and prefer defined risk.

when.iv: IV rises into the report and drops sharply after; tastylive sells premium before the announcement and buys it back afterward to harvest the crush [page:concepts-earnings] [page:concepts-iv-crush]. Elevated IV may reflect a real chance of a gap, so selling it is not always right [page:concepts-iv-crush].
when.outlook: Volatility, not direction: avoid directional earnings bets, since stocks can fall on beats and rise on misses [page:concepts-earnings].
when.events: The trade is the event. Check the stock's historical earnings reactions first, since high IV often signals a real move [ep:research-2024-10-21@06:41].

avoid: Directional earnings bets [page:concepts-earnings].
Names that rarely move on earnings (such as pharma) and illiquid chains [ep:research-2024-10-21@07:51].
Buying options with elevated IV ahead of a known event: a crush can lose money even when direction is right [page:concepts-iv-crush].
Buying earnings options at retail spreads near 20% of price [lit:desilva-etal-2025].
Bellwether names whose reports raise market-wide volatility: straddle returns around them are predictably lower for the buyer, so the seller is paid a market-wide risk premium [lit:barth-so-2014].

setup.dte: Not specified in the study [ep:research-2024-10-21@01:45]. Sell before the announcement and buy back after [page:concepts-earnings].
setup.strikes: 16-delta strangle, or 16-delta shorts with 10-delta wings (condor) [ep:research-2024-10-21@01:45] [ep:research-2024-10-21@03:19].
setup.credit_target: No tastylive guidance found in the reviewed pages; no credit target.
setup.underlying: Liquid large caps; the tastylive study used AAPL, NFLX, AMZN and TSLA [ep:research-2024-10-21@01:45]. Vendor data show the event premium richest in large caps [lit:ivolatility-2026].

manage.profit_target: No tastylive guidance found in the reviewed pages; no profit-target rule for earnings.
manage.time_exit: Buy the position back after the announcement [page:concepts-earnings]. Hosts also prefer post-earnings trades over entering before the report [ep:options-jive-2026-02-09@13:36].
manage.roll: No tastylive guidance found in the reviewed pages; no roll guidance for earnings.
manage.defend: Set entry and exit points for positive, neutral and negative scenarios, update as news arrives, and reassess after the report [page:concepts-how-to-trade-earnings-with-options].
manage.loss_rule: Analyze the worst case before the trade and either pass or add structure to limit it [page:concepts-iv-crush]; use defined risk if markets are wide [ep:research-2024-10-21@07:51].

size.per_trade: Keep earnings positions small because moves can be large and unpredictable [ep:research-2024-10-21@07:02]; under about 5% of the account [page:concepts-number-of-occurrences].
size.notes: Direction is essentially a coin flip, so keep earnings trades small or skip them [ep:options-jive-2026-02-09@13:36]. Scale back and trade smaller [page:concepts-how-to-trade-earnings-with-options]. IRA accounts allow defined-risk spreads, not naked strangles [lit:tastytrade-ira-2026].

cards.name: Short put
cards.one_liner: Sell an out-of-the-money put with no cash or hedge behind it; you are paid for implied volatility running above what the market realizes and for taking the obligation to buy 100 shares per contract below the strike, with a large but finite loss if the stock collapses.

when.iv: tastylive: IV rank above 50 favors selling premium [page:concepts-implied-volatility-rank-percentile]. The literature finds the index premium shows no significant link to the IV level and is lower after sell-offs on a risk-sized basis [lit:fallon-park-2016].
when.outlook: Neutral to bullish (sideways or higher) [page:concepts-naked-options] [page:concepts-put-options].
when.events: Gaps from binary events (regulatory decisions, M&A, disasters) are not contained by stops [page:concepts-risk-management]; no event-specific rule for short puts in the reviewed pages.

avoid: Stocks you would not be willing to own at the strike: assignment puts you long 100 shares per contract below the strike [page:concepts-naked-options] [page:concepts-put-options].
Low IV: a trade in IWM at IV rank 8.4 was called poor premium efficiency [ep:from-theory-to-practice-2022-12-21@16:01].
IRA and cash accounts: naked puts are not allowed (cash-secured puts are the allowed version) [lit:tastytrade-ira-2026].
Beginners and small accounts: tastylive says paper trade naked options first [page:concepts-naked-options].
Single stocks with an unusually steep put smirk: it has been a bearish signal for the stock, not free premium [lit:xing-etal-2010].
Illiquid underlyings and strikes [page:concepts-options-liquidity].

setup.dte: About 45 days: tastylive research on short options found 45 DTE balances decay speed with premium collected [page:concepts-options-expiration]. No short-put-specific DTE on the reviewed pages.
setup.strikes: No short-put strike or delta rule on the reviewed pages. Reference point: a strike with about a 16% chance of finishing in the money marks one standard deviation [page:concepts-standard-deviation]; in high IV the same-probability strike sits farther from the stock [page:concepts-implied-volatility].
setup.credit_target: No tastylive guidance found in the reviewed pages. Efficiency yardstick from one episode: theta around 0.1% of net liquidity [ep:from-theory-to-practice-2022-12-21@16:01].
setup.underlying: Liquid index products carry the sourced premium: index implied variance has exceeded realized on average [lit:carr-wu-2009], but the single-stock variance premium was significant in level terms for only 3 of 35 names [lit:carr-wu-2009]. For single names, tastylive says pick a stock you would buy at the strike [page:concepts-naked-options].

manage.profit_target: Close winners at about 50% of max profit [page:concepts-managing-winners].
manage.time_exit: tastylive's 21-DTE exit test on SPY naked puts and strangles: largest losses down almost 50% versus holding [lit:tastylive-cutlosses-nd].
manage.roll: Roll out in time only for a net credit, about 7-21 days before expiration; paying to roll worsens breakeven [page:concepts-defending-positions]. A deep in-the-money assigned put acts like about 100 deltas of stock; a bullish holder can keep the shares and sell calls [ep:from-theory-to-practice-2022-12-21@11:29].
manage.defend: tastylive: have a plan if the price nears or falls through the strike (buy back, or fund the purchase) [page:concepts-naked-options].
manage.loss_rule: tastylive: close at a net loss of 2x the credit received [page:concepts-defending-positions]. The literature finds a simple stop-loss has a negative expected effect under a random walk and fills slipped past stops in Feb 2018 [lit:kaminski-lo-2014].

size.bpr_formula: Naked put (Reg T): premium + max(20% of underlying - OTM amount, 10% of strike) x 100; 15% instead of 20% for broad indexes such as SPX/XSP [lit:finra-4210-2026]. tastylive's rule of thumb: about 20% of the strike [page:concepts-notional-value]. Portfolio margin uses stress tests: -8%/+6% for high-cap broad indexes, +/-15% for equities, plus tastytrade's own house stress [lit:finra-4210-2026] [lit:tastytrade-pm-2026].
size.per_trade: Keep each trade under about 5% of the account [page:concepts-number-of-occurrences]; the general primer suggests risking about 1% per trade, 2% if aggressive [page:concepts-risk-management].
size.notes: Use 25-50% of buying power across all positions, never above 75% [ep:options-jive-2023-12-27@06:56]. Size as equity risk: put-write beta to the S&P 500 is about 0.56-0.60 [lit:bondarenko-2019] [repro:cboe_short_vol]. Posted margin is not maximum loss: portfolio-margin stresses are only -8%/+6% on high-cap indexes, so gap losses can exceed BPR [lit:finra-4210-2026]. Half Kelly or less is the defensible fraction for negatively skewed payoffs [lit:thorp-2006] [lit:maclean-etal-2010].

The literature finds a simple stop has a negative expected effect under a random walk [lit:kaminski-lo-2014].

size.bpr_formula: Naked call (Reg T): premium + max(20% of underlying - OTM amount, 10% of underlying) x 100; 15% instead of 20% for broad indexes such as SPX/XSP [lit:finra-4210-2026]. Broker-specific and may be higher [page:concepts-naked-options]. Portfolio margin uses stress tests: +/-15% for equities, -8%/+6% for high-cap broad indexes, plus tastytrade's house stress [lit:finra-4210-2026] [lit:tastytrade-pm-2026].
size.per_trade: Keep each trade under about 5% of the account [page:concepts-number-of-occurrences]; the general primer suggests about 1% risk per trade, 2% if aggressive [page:concepts-risk-management]. With unlimited loss, budget the loss at a stress price, not at the margin posted.
size.notes: Use 25-50% of buying power across all positions, never above 75% [ep:options-jive-2023-12-27@06:56]. Posted margin is not maximum loss: portfolio-margin stresses are only -8%/+6% on high-cap indexes [lit:finra-4210-2026]. Short-vol blow-ups combined leverage or concentration with a stated worst case far below the loss; OptionSellers' short natural-gas calls left $35.3M of deficit claims after liquidation [lit:famag-optionsellers-2018] [lit:thinkadvisor-optionsellers-2018].

cards.name: Jade lizard
cards.one_liner: Sell an out-of-the-money put and an out-of-the-money call spread in one expiration for a credit larger than the call spread's width, so there is no upside risk and all the risk sits on the downside put.

when.iv: High IV rank, such as a stock that has sold off [page:concepts-jade-lizard]; IV rank above 50 is tastylive's sell zone [page:concepts-implied-volatility-rank-percentile]. Conflict: for single stocks the literature finds steep put skew is a bearish signal, not free premium (steepest-smirk stocks lagged by 10.9%/yr risk-adjusted) [lit:xing-etal-2010].
when.outlook: Neutral to slightly bullish, not extremely bullish [page:concepts-jade-lizard]; the host's use is mildly bullish or on the fence, where it adds cushion versus a naked put [ep:market-measures-2026-05-02-2@02:10]. Also suggested for a bullish view on a name with call skew and elevated vol [ep:options-jive-2026-02-09@06:07].
when.events: No tastylive guidance found in the reviewed pages.

avoid: An extremely bullish view, and traders new to options [page:concepts-jade-lizard].
Credit smaller than the call spread width: that leaves upside risk [page:concepts-jade-lizard].
IRA and cash accounts for the naked-put form: naked puts are not allowed in IRAs [lit:tastytrade-ira-2026]; the put-wing form is defined risk (see variants).
Illiquid underlyings: several legs need liquid strikes [page:concepts-options-liquidity].

setup.dte: tastylive's only jade lizard study used short-dated SPX entries; 5 to 7 days to expiration won, and 10 days added almost no P&L while holding longer [ep:market-measures-2026-05-02-2@06:36] [ep:market-measures-2026-05-02-2@03:47]. The jade lizard page gives no DTE [page:concepts-jade-lizard]. General (not jade-specific) short-option research favored 45 DTE [page:concepts-options-expiration].
setup.strikes: Short strikes at the expected move; study widths were a $20 put spread with a $5 call spread, or a $30 put spread with a $10 call spread; a wider put spread raised P&L, and a wider call spread did not hurt while the put spread was wide [ep:market-measures-2026-05-02-2@03:47]. A strike with a 16% chance of finishing ITM marks about 1 standard deviation [page:concepts-standard-deviation].
setup.credit_target: Total credit greater than the call spread width [page:concepts-jade-lizard].
setup.underlying: SPX in the study [ep:market-measures-2026-05-02-2@03:47]; the page says a stock or ETF with a neutral-to-bullish view [page:concepts-jade-lizard].

manage.profit_target: Short-dated SPX study: close at 25% of max profit to free capital for redeployment; a 50% target usually meant holding to expiration [ep:market-measures-2026-05-02-2@11:03]. The page gives no target [page:concepts-jade-lizard].
manage.time_exit: No tastylive guidance found in the reviewed pages for a time exit on this strategy.
manage.roll: If price nears a short strike and the thesis holds, roll out in time and optionally to new strikes [page:concepts-jade-lizard]; general tastylive rule: roll only for a net credit, about 7-21 days before expiration [page:concepts-defending-positions].
manage.defend: Exit by buying back the put and the call spread, or let expire if both are OTM; the short put or short call may be assigned shares at its strike [page:concepts-jade-lizard].
manage.loss_rule: No jade-lizard loss rule on the page [page:concepts-jade-lizard]. tastylive's general premium-selling rule is to close at a net loss of 2x the credit [page:concepts-defending-positions]; it was not tested on jade lizards.

size.bpr_formula: Naked-put form (Reg T): the put leg follows the FINRA formula, premium + max(20% of underlying - OTM amount, 10% of strike floor) x 100, with 15% instead of 20% for broad indexes [lit:finra-4210-2026]; how the call spread adds to it is not yet verified. Put-wing form (defined risk): larger spread width x 100 minus the credit; combined-leg rule not yet verified. Portfolio margin uses stress tests [lit:tastytrade-pm-2026].
size.per_trade: Keep each trade under about 5% of the account [page:concepts-number-of-occurrences].
size.notes: Use 25-50% of buying power across all positions, never above 75% [ep:options-jive-2023-12-27@06:56]. Size the put as equity risk: short index puts carry a beta of about 0.56-0.60 [lit:bondarenko-2019]. Buying a put wing in SPX instead of selling the put naked sharply cuts buying power [ep:market-measures-2026-05-02-2@05:45]. A put-heavy structure is a bigger bet on the same crash factor, not diversification [lit:kozhan-etal-2013].

cards.name: Ratio spread
cards.one_liner: Buy one option and sell two further-out options of the same type for a net credit; it peaks if the stock pins the short strike, has no risk on one side, and carries undefined risk beyond the breakeven on the other.

greeks.delta: put front ratio starts long delta; call front ratio starts short delta [page:concepts-ratio-spread]

when.iv: High IV preferred: richer far-OTM premium lets the embedded spread be wider and still take a credit; avoid low IV, where the spread must be very narrow [page:concepts-ratio-spread].
when.outlook: Put front ratio neutral to bearish with no upside risk; call front ratio neutral to bullish with no downside risk; you need a price target for the underlying [page:concepts-ratio-spread].
when.events: No tastylive guidance found in the reviewed pages.

avoid: Low implied volatility [page:concepts-ratio-spread].
Back ratios for a debit: tastylive does not normally route them; the front ratio is the go-to [page:concepts-ratio-spread].
Ignoring the price level the underlying must not breach, since risk is undefined past breakeven [page:concepts-ratio-spread].
IRA and cash accounts: the extra short put is naked and naked puts are not allowed in IRAs; uncovered calls need The Works tier plus $25,000 start-of-day net liquidation [lit:tastytrade-ira-2026].

setup.dte: No tastylive guidance found in the reviewed pages for ratio spread DTE. General (not ratio-specific) short-option research favored 45 DTE [page:concepts-options-expiration].
setup.strikes: Put the short strike at the price target, since max profit comes there; a wider embedded spread gives a better breakeven; put the shorts on the skewed side for a wider spread or more credit [page:concepts-ratio-spread].
setup.credit_target: Route for a net credit so the OTM side has no risk; the credit is the profit if it expires OTM [page:concepts-ratio-spread]. Worked example: $1.60 credit on a 2-wide vertical [ep:from-theory-to-practice-2023-03-20@09:16].
setup.underlying: Put-skewed products make put front ratios wider or better than calls [page:concepts-ratio-spread]; liquid symbols [page:concepts-options-liquidity].

manage.time_exit: Close early rather than hold for the last bit of premium, to avoid gamma risk; the example had about 21 days left [ep:from-theory-to-practice-2023-03-20@11:06].
manage.roll: Roll the whole spread out, or roll only the naked short while selling the long spread near max value; the extra short can be rolled to the next month for duration [page:concepts-ratio-spread].
manage.defend: If the long vertical can be sold near max value, sell it and keep the extra short, rolling that short if more duration is wanted; if assigned on the extra short call, convert to a covered put, and if on the extra short put, to a covered call [page:concepts-ratio-spread].
manage.loss_rule: No ratio-spread loss rule on the page. tastylive's general premium-selling rule is a close at a net loss of 2x the credit [page:concepts-defending-positions]; it was not tested on ratio spreads.

Portfolio margin uses stress tests [lit:tastytrade-pm-2026].

cards.name: Butterfly
cards.one_liner: Buy one option on each outer strike and sell two at the middle strike, all calls or all puts: a cheap, defined-risk bet that the stock sits near the middle strike at expiration, with a low chance of the full payoff.

greeks.vega: - near the middle strike (structure); tastylive buys it in high IV because the structure then costs less [page:concepts-long-butterfly-spread]

The literature points the other way for long premium on the index: delta-hedged long S&P 500 options lose on average, and more when volatility is high [lit:bakshi-kapadia-2003].
when.outlook: Neutral: little or no movement, with the stock finishing at the middle strike [page:concepts-long-butterfly-spread].
when.events: No tastylive guidance found in the reviewed pages.

cards.name: Broken-wing butterfly
cards.one_liner: A butterfly with one wing placed farther away, routed for a small credit so nothing is lost if everything expires out of the money; the risk sits only on the wide-wing side, and it is defined.

greeks.delta: slightly directional: calls lean up, puts lean down for the profit zone [page:concepts-broken-wing-butterfly]

when.iv: tastylive: high IV rank and high IV; the trade benefits from volatility contraction [page:concepts-broken-wing-butterfly]. Index implied volatility has exceeded realized on average (the premium being sold) [lit:ungar-moran-2009], but defined-risk wings gave up most of it (Cboe CNDR 0.98% CAGR 2007-2026, below T-bills at 1.56%) [repro:cboe_short_vol]. No test of this structure's IV rank filter.
when.outlook: Neutral to slightly directional; the profit zone leans the way of the wing (calls up, puts down) [page:concepts-broken-wing-butterfly]. Pitched as a way to get a higher chance of profit than a regular butterfly, or a defined-risk alternative to a ratio spread [page:concepts-broken-wing-butterfly].
when.events: No tastylive guidance found in the reviewed pages.

avoid: Entering for a debit: it removes the no-loss-when-out-of-the-money advantage [page:concepts-broken-wing-butterfly].
Holding it partly in the money through expiration, where unwanted shares can result [page:concepts-broken-wing-butterfly].
A move through the wide wing: maximum loss is the wide-spread width minus the narrow width minus the credit [page:concepts-broken-wing-butterfly].

setup.dte: No tastylive guidance found in the reviewed pages.
setup.strikes: All calls or all puts: a narrow debit spread (at- or out-of-the-money) plus a wider credit spread further out, sharing the short strike; the narrow side is narrower than the broken wing [page:concepts-broken-wing-butterfly]. No delta guidance found.
setup.credit_target: Always route for a credit, usually a very small one [page:concepts-broken-wing-butterfly] [page:concepts-10-options-strategies-every-trader-should-know].
setup.underlying: No tastylive guidance found in the reviewed pages.

manage.profit_target: Aim for 50% of max profit rather than closing for a minor gain; an FAQ in the same page cites 25% [page:concepts-broken-wing-butterfly]. The 50% level is reached roughly when the closest long goes in the money near expiration (page's rough estimate: the distance between the closest long and the shorts divided by two, or by four for 25%) [page:concepts-broken-wing-butterfly].
manage.time_exit: If partly in the money near expiration, close rather than hold [page:concepts-broken-wing-butterfly]. No DTE-based exit found.
manage.roll: Roll the remaining short spread out in time only if it can be done for a credit: this lowers max loss, raises max profit and adds time [page:concepts-broken-wing-butterfly].
manage.defend: If it goes against you, separate the spreads: close the long spread for its maximum value and use it to cut the cost basis of the tested short spread [page:concepts-broken-wing-butterfly].
manage.loss_rule: No fixed stop found in the reviewed BWB pages. The generic tastylive premium-selling rule is to close at a net loss of 2x the credit [page:concepts-defending-positions], but the credit here is very small, so that rule is not set up for this structure (not tested).

size.bpr_formula: Maximum loss x 100 = (wide spread width - narrow spread width - credit) x 100 [page:concepts-broken-wing-butterfly]. tastylive says the buying power is relatively low versus many strategies but gives no formula [page:concepts-broken-wing-butterfly]; the broker requirement is not yet verified.
size.per_trade: Keep each trade under about 5% of the account [page:concepts-number-of-occurrences]; size by the maximum loss, not by the small credit.
size.notes: Use 25-50% of buying power across all positions, never above 75% [ep:options-jive-2023-12-27@06:56]. Cash account: not fully secured by the credit (needs margin), so false; IRA: defined-risk spreads are allowed in tastytrade Basic and The Works [lit:tastytrade-ira-2026]. Portfolio margin needs a margin account at The Works level [lit:tastytrade-pm-2026].

conventions.effect: Removes the loss on the narrow side if everything expires out of the money and raises the win rate; pushes the risk onto the wide wing, so the tail is a single-direction loss [page:concepts-broken-wing-butterfly].

conventions.rule: Take profit at 50% (or 25%) of max profit
conventions.effect: Raises the win rate and turnover, caps winners; no test in the reviewed sources [page:concepts-broken-wing-butterfly] [page:concepts-managing-winners].

conventions.effect: Lowers max loss and adds time; defers a loss rather than removing it [page:concepts-broken-wing-butterfly] [page:concepts-defending-positions].

Holding partly in the money into expiration and ending up with shares [page:concepts-broken-wing-butterfly].
Closing for a tiny profit because the credits are small [page:concepts-broken-wing-butterfly].

cards.name: Covered call
cards.one_liner: Own 100 shares and sell one out-of-the-money call against them for income; you keep the premium and give up the upside above the strike, while the downside on the shares stays almost fully yours.

when.iv: tastylive: high IV is the ideal environment [page:concepts-covered-call]; consider short-premium structures including covered calls when IV is high, because the same premium sits at strikes farther from the stock [page:concepts-implied-volatility]. When volatility is low the hosts say they shift toward covered calls, ATM debit spreads, diagonals or calendars [ep:market-measures-2025-12-19@04:24]. These two readings differ: one wants rich IV, the other uses covered calls as a low-vol fallback.
when.outlook: Neutral to slightly bullish: you expect sideways or modestly higher and are willing to be sold out at the strike [page:concepts-covered-call].
when.events: Single events: covered calls are listed as a way to earn extra income into earnings if the stock trades sideways or slightly higher, with some cushion in a selloff [page:concepts-how-to-trade-earnings-with-options]. For stock headed for long-term holding status, only qualified covered calls (listed, more than 30 days to expiry, not deep in the money) avoid straddle loss deferral [lit:irs-p550-2025].

avoid: Being very bullish on the stock: the short call caps the upside [page:concepts-covered-call].
Thin premium: if the call would pay only about $0.10, tastylive says to wait or use another strategy [page:concepts-covered-call].
Shares you are not willing to sell at the strike (assignment hands them over at the strike; the upside above is forfeited) [page:concepts-covered-call].
Rolling the call down below your current breakeven: it can lock in a loss if the stock rebounds [page:concepts-covered-call].
Treating it as downside protection: the max loss is the stock going to zero, cushioned only by the credit [page:concepts-covered-call].

setup.dte: About 45 DTE, which tastylive calls ideal per its studies [page:concepts-covered-call].
setup.strikes: Sell the most liquid call near 30 delta [page:concepts-covered-call]. Strike choice by view: far OTM keeps upside, about 35-40 delta collects more premium, ATM maximizes extrinsic value [ep:from-theory-to-practice-2022-12-21@29:48]. Literature: in 1990-2005 BXM data, writing 2% OTM calls dominated ATM because it gave up less of the equity premium [lit:hill-etal-2006].
setup.credit_target: The credit must be meaningful; an example of about $0.10 is called too small [page:concepts-covered-call]. No other fixed credit target found in the reviewed pages.
setup.underlying: tastylive favors low-priced, high-volatility stocks [page:concepts-covered-call]. Liquidity matters: pick the most liquid strike [page:concepts-options-liquidity].

manage.profit_target: No percentage profit target for covered calls on the reviewed pages. Close when the stock has moved well beyond the short strike, which is near max profit [page:concepts-covered-call]. (The generic 50% rule applies to premium-selling trades in general [page:concepts-managing-winners].)
manage.time_exit: No fixed time exit for covered calls found. Generic guidance for rolling short options is 7-21 days before expiration to avoid growing gamma and assignment risk [page:concepts-defending-positions].
manage.roll: If the thesis is unchanged and little extrinsic value remains, buy the call back and sell the same strike further out in time [page:concepts-covered-call]. To avoid being called away, roll out, up, or both [page:concepts-10-options-strategies-every-trader-should-know]. Roll for a credit only [page:concepts-defending-positions].
manage.defend: If the stock falls, roll the call down to collect more credit, lowering max loss and breakeven, but never below the current breakeven [page:concepts-covered-call].
manage.loss_rule: Consider closing if the stock falls a lot and your assumption changes [page:concepts-covered-call]. No fixed multiple-of-credit stop applies: the 2x-credit rule on the defending page is for premium-selling trades in general [page:concepts-defending-positions] and does not describe the share-side loss.

size.bpr_formula: Stock-based: the position costs 100 x share price less the call credit; the shares are the collateral, so the short call needs no extra margin (standard structure, source for the margin treatment not yet verified). Reg T initial margin on the shares is 50% [lit:frb-regt-220-12-nd]. In cash and IRA accounts the shares are paid in full [lit:tastytrade-ira-2026].
size.per_trade: Keep each trade under about 5% of the account [page:concepts-number-of-occurrences]; generic risk guidance is about 1% (up to 2%) of the portfolio at risk per trade, though the covered call's risk is the stock itself [page:concepts-risk-management].
size.notes: Part of the 25-50% options sleeve, never above 75% of buying power [ep:options-jive-2023-12-27@06:56]. Size it as equity risk: BXM beta is about 0.62-0.67 and BXMD about 0.80 [lit:israelov-nielsen-2014] [repro:cboe_short_vol]. Do not count the premium as extra return; most of the risk is the stock.

evidence.note: Covered calls collect a real but small volatility premium; most of the return and risk is equity beta, and since 2009 BXM trailed the S&P 500 TR on both CAGR and Sharpe [lit:israelov-nielsen-2014] [repro:cboe_short_vol]. tastylive's 45-DTE, 30-delta, high-IV setup [page:concepts-covered-call] has no episode study in the reviewed material; the index evidence (monthly ATM for BXM, 30-delta for BXMD) is the closest independent test. The benefit is lower volatility and a shallower drawdown, not extra return. The index studies are mostly Cboe-sponsored.

conventions.rule: Sell about 30 delta, 45 DTE
conventions.effect: Sets the trade-off between premium and upside given up; BXMD (30 delta) had higher CAGR and beta than BXM (ATM) over 2007-2026 because it keeps more equity exposure [repro:cboe_short_vol] [lit:hill-etal-2006]. Not a separate source of return.

conventions.rule: Roll out (and up) for a credit before assignment
conventions.effect: Delays being called away and keeps the share exposure; a roll is economically a close plus a new trade, so it adds no edge by itself [page:concepts-covered-call] [lit:williams-1991].

conventions.rule: Roll the call down after a drop, never below breakeven
conventions.effect: Raises income and lowers breakeven, but caps the rebound and shifts risk toward locking a loss if the stock recovers [page:concepts-covered-call].

mistakes: Selling calls on a stock you are very bullish on: the cap costs you the move [page:concepts-covered-call].
Rolling the call down past breakeven, then watching the stock rebound through the strike [page:concepts-covered-call].
Selling a tiny-premium call (about $0.10) that is not worth the capped upside [page:concepts-covered-call].
Believing the premium is free return: only about 11% of it is volatility compensation, the rest is equity exposure given back and reshaped [lit:israelov-nielsen-2014].
Ignoring tax rules on held stock: non-qualified covered calls can trigger straddle loss deferral, and replacement purchases in an IRA can permanently disallow a taxable loss [lit:irs-p550-2025].

variants.name: Covered strangle
variants.how_it_differs: Adds a short out-of-the-money put to a covered call, so you hold shares, sell a call above and a put below. It collects more premium but doubles down on the stock if it falls, and the short put is an additional undefined-risk obligation, not allowed in cash or IRA accounts as a naked put [lit:tastytrade-ira-2026]. No tastylive guidance on the strategy was found in the reviewed covered-call pages; it appeared in 6 archive episodes, mostly 2012-2016.

cards.name: Collar
cards.one_liner: Own 100 shares, buy an out-of-the-money put and sell an out-of-the-money call in the same expiration: the call premium funds the put, and in exchange you accept capped upside for a floor under the stock.

greeks.theta: roughly offsetting (long put, short call; structure)
greeks.vega: roughly offsetting (long put, short call; structure)

when.iv: No tastylive guidance found in the reviewed pages.
when.outlook: Protective on a stock you want to keep (taxes, dividends, long-term view), when you expect near-term volatility or a correction [page:concepts-collar-option]; also after a big run-up to protect gains, or around earnings season [page:concepts-10-options-strategies-every-trader-should-know].
when.events: Earnings season is named as a use case [page:concepts-10-options-strategies-every-trader-should-know].

avoid: When a strong rally is expected, since the upside is capped at the call strike [page:concepts-collar-option].
Paying a net debit because the put costs more than the call [page:concepts-collar-option].
Treating it as a free hedge: rolling index puts cost about 3 points of CAGR a year in the proxy test [repro:cboe_tail_hedge].

setup.dte: Same expiration for both options, chosen per outlook; no tastylive DTE guidance found [page:concepts-collar-option].
setup.strikes: Put below and call above the current price; the ideal is a cost-neutral collar where the call credit roughly equals the put cost [page:concepts-collar-option]. No delta guidance found.
setup.credit_target: About zero net cost [page:concepts-collar-option].
setup.underlying: 100 shares per collar for full protection; a collar may cover only part of the position, leaving the rest unprotected [page:concepts-collar-option].

manage.profit_target: No tastylive guidance found in the reviewed pages.
manage.time_exit: Close the options or let them expire [page:concepts-collar-option].
manage.roll: No tastylive guidance found in the reviewed pages.
manage.defend: No tastylive guidance found in the reviewed pages.
manage.loss_rule: The put sets the floor: maximum loss is (entry price - put strike) adjusted for net premium, times 100 [page:concepts-collar-option].

size.bpr_formula: Stock cost (Reg T initial margin 50% on margin equity securities if bought on margin) [lit:frb-regt-220-12-nd]; the long put and the share-covered short call add no naked-option requirement (structure; broker treatment not yet verified).
size.per_trade: Hedge only the shares that matter; one contract per 100 shares for full protection, fewer for partial [page:concepts-collar-option]. Keep individual positions small [page:concepts-number-of-occurrences].
size.notes: Trading smaller can substitute: a 56% S&P 500 / 44% T-bill mix matched the PPUT put-overlay's CAGR (7.92%) with a -31.5% max drawdown vs -38.9% [repro:cboe_tail_hedge]. Accounts: covered calls and long options are allowed in tastytrade IRAs [lit:tastytrade-ira-2026]; shares are required, so cash accounts work when fully paid.

evidence.note: tastylive's two pages describe the structure and uses but give no numbers, study or management rules. The independent evidence is that a collar is insurance, not a return source: the put leg costs about 3 points a year in index tests [repro:cboe_tail_hedge] [lit:bondarenko-2019] and protected portfolios had worse tail losses than equal-return stock/cash mixes [lit:israelov-2018]; the Cboe CLL index cut drawdown and beta but gave up a large share of the return, and a dedicated collar paper was not read [lit:israelov-klein-2016].

conventions.rule: Balance the put cost against the call credit (zero-cost collar)
conventions.effect: Removes the premium outlay and caps the upside; the cost is paid in forgone gains instead of cash [page:concepts-collar-option] [repro:cboe_tail_hedge].

conventions.rule: Hedge only part of the position
conventions.effect: Reduces the cap and the protection proportionally; unhedged shares keep upside and risk [page:concepts-collar-option].

mistakes: Letting the put cost more than the call, creating a net debit [page:concepts-collar-option].
Choosing strikes by misjudging volatility [page:concepts-collar-option].
Partial coverage leaves the uncovered shares unprotected [page:concepts-collar-option].
Expecting the collar to protect every month: the CLL index's worst month was worse than the S&P 500's in the since-2009 window [repro:cboe_tail_hedge].

cards.name: Poor man's covered call
cards.one_liner: Buy a deep in-the-money long-dated call and sell a shorter-dated out-of-the-money call against it: a covered call built with far less capital, with the long call standing in for the shares.

greeks.vega: mixed (long-dated long call is long vega, short call is short vega)

when.iv: tastylive's page lists low IV as the ideal environment [page:concepts-poor-man-covered-call].
when.outlook: Neutral to bullish, a moderately bullish or neutral long-term view on a stock or ETF [page:concepts-poor-man-covered-call].
when.events: No tastylive guidance found in the reviewed pages on earnings or other events. Watch dividends: an ITM short call near an ex-dividend date raises early-assignment risk [page:concepts-poor-man-covered-call].

avoid: Volatility instruments: each expiration acts as its own underlying, so the max loss is not defined [page:concepts-poor-man-covered-call].
Setups where the short call's premium is below the long call's extrinsic value, or the total debit exceeds 75% of the strike width [page:concepts-poor-man-covered-call].
Ignoring early assignment when the short call goes in the money, especially around dividends [page:concepts-poor-man-covered-call].
Very bullish views: gains above the short strike are given up [page:concepts-poor-man-covered-call].

setup.dte: Short call typically 30-60 days out; long call several months to years out (a LEAP) [page:concepts-poor-man-covered-call].
setup.strikes: Long call deep in the money with high delta; short call out of the money [page:concepts-poor-man-covered-call]. No specific delta values given on the reviewed page.
setup.credit_target: This is a debit trade: keep the total debit at or below 75% of the strike width, and sell a short call worth at least the long call's extrinsic value [page:concepts-poor-man-covered-call].
setup.underlying: Stocks and ETFs; never volatility instruments [page:concepts-poor-man-covered-call]. Needs liquid options across several strikes and expirations [page:concepts-options-liquidity].

manage.profit_target: No percentage target specific to the PMCC. tastylive manages calendars and diagonals between 10% and 50% of max profit [page:concepts-managing-winners]; the PMCC is described as a long call diagonal [page:concepts-poor-man-covered-call], but the page does not say that range applies to it.
manage.time_exit: Near short-call expiry, let it expire, buy it back, or roll it later or to another strike [page:concepts-poor-man-covered-call]. Generic rolling window for short options is 7-21 days before expiration [page:concepts-defending-positions].
manage.roll: Roll the short call for a credit only [page:concepts-defending-positions]. If the stock fell, roll the short call to a lower strike for more credit [page:concepts-poor-man-covered-call].
manage.defend: If the short call is assigned, either exercise the deep ITM long call to get shares that offset the short stock, or buy shares in the market and sell the long call [page:concepts-poor-man-covered-call].
manage.loss_rule: No fixed loss rule found on the PMCC page. After a sharp one-cycle rally, options trade near intrinsic value and little profit remains, so close the winner [page:concepts-poor-man-covered-call].

size.bpr_formula: Defined-risk debit: net debit paid x 100 (long call cost minus short call credit); the debit is the max loss [page:concepts-poor-man-covered-call]. Margin treatment of the diagonal in a margin account not yet verified.
size.per_trade: Keep each trade under about 5% of the account [page:concepts-number-of-occurrences].
size.notes: Part of the 25-50% options sleeve, never above 75% of buying power [ep:options-jive-2023-12-27@06:56]. Page notes it is useful in smaller accounts to mimic a covered call with far less capital and risk [page:concepts-poor-man-covered-call]. IRAs allow defined-risk spreads [lit:tastytrade-ira-2026]; whether a tastytrade IRA tier accepts this particular diagonal was not verified, and cash accounts are marked false because the short call is covered by a long call of a different expiration (not yet verified).

cards.name: LEAPS / deep-ITM stock replacement
cards.one_liner: Buy a deep in-the-money call at least a year out instead of 100 shares: stock-like upside for a fraction of the capital, with the loss capped at the premium paid.

when.iv: No tastylive IV guidance for the LEAPS page; the ZEBRA variant prefers low IV [page:concepts-zebra].
when.outlook: Bullish on the long-term prospects of the stock, with less capital than owning shares [page:concepts-leaps].
when.events: No tastylive guidance found in the reviewed pages.

avoid: A stock that moves slowly or not as expected: the LEAPS can underperform the shares [page:concepts-leaps].
Illiquid contracts: check open interest and volume; LEAPS are less liquid than near-term options [page:concepts-leaps].
Paying extra extrinsic value to get a cheaper trade: it decays and dampens profit as the trade moves ITM (ZEBRA page) [page:concepts-zebra].

setup.dte: Expirations at least one year out, up to two or three years [page:concepts-leaps].
setup.strikes: Deep in the money; the page example is a 70-strike call on a $100 stock for a premium of 35 [page:concepts-leaps]. No target delta given on the reviewed page.
setup.credit_target: Debit trade: pay as little extrinsic value as possible. Nothing more specific found.
setup.underlying: Stocks and ETFs you would own; the example in the ZEBRA variant is SPY [page:concepts-zebra]. Pick the contract with high open interest [page:concepts-leaps].

manage.profit_target: No profit target found for LEAPS. Calendars and diagonals are managed between 10% and 50% of max profit [page:concepts-managing-winners], but that does not describe a long-dated stock substitute.
manage.time_exit: Near expiration, sell the LEAP and buy a later-dated one to extend [page:concepts-leaps]. If ITM near expiry, sell or exercise; if OTM and unlikely to recover, let it expire [page:concepts-leaps].
manage.roll: Sell the LEAP near expiration and buy a later one [page:concepts-leaps].
manage.defend: No tastylive guidance found in the reviewed pages.
manage.loss_rule: Max loss is the premium paid; the page notes you can sell or exercise before expiration to lock gains or cut losses [page:concepts-leaps]. No stop-loss rule given.

size.bpr_formula: Long option, defined risk: premium paid x 100 (the debit is the max loss) [page:concepts-leaps].
size.per_trade: Keep each trade under about 5% of the account [page:concepts-number-of-occurrences]; generic risk guidance is about 1% (up to 2%) per trade [page:concepts-risk-management]. Because the LEAPS is stock-like, size by the delta-equivalent share exposure, not the premium alone.
size.notes: Part of the 25-50% options sleeve [ep:options-jive-2023-12-27@06:56]. Long options can be held in cash accounts and IRAs [lit:tastytrade-ira-2026]. Broker options approval is required [page:concepts-leaps].

variants.how_it_differs: Buy two ITM calls and sell one ATM call so the short's extrinsic cancels the longs', giving about 100 delta with a debit-limited loss and (properly built) no extrinsic to decay; best in low IV, short-dated for brief moves, longer-dated for long-term tax treatment [page:concepts-zebra] [page:concepts-ratio-spread].

cards.name: Calendar spread
cards.one_liner: Sell a near-term option and buy a longer-dated option at the same strike: a cheap, debit-limited bet that the stock stays near the strike while the short leg decays faster and implied volatility holds or rises.

greeks.theta: + while the stock is near the strikes

when.iv: tastylive: only the lowest-IV environments; it is a pure extrinsic trade that benefits from an IV rise [page:concepts-calendar-spread]. Consider long-premium structures including calendars when IV is low and options are cheap [page:concepts-implied-volatility]; when volatility is low the hosts shift toward covered calls, ATM debit spreads, diagonals or calendars [ep:market-measures-2025-12-19@04:24].
when.outlook: Neutral; slightly bullish with an OTM call calendar, slightly bearish with an OTM put calendar [page:concepts-calendar-spread].
when.events: The earnings page lists a calendar (short nearest monthly, long the next) as a way to profit from the post-earnings volatility crush with the stock near the strike [page:concepts-how-to-trade-earnings-with-options]. Note this differs from the low-IV rule above: the earnings use sells the elevated front-month IV, while the concept page says to trade only in the lowest IV [page:concepts-calendar-spread].

avoid: Stocks that move far from the strike: the trade loses when the stock leaves the strike area [page:concepts-calendar-spread].
Volatility instruments: each expiration acts as its own underlying, so max loss is not defined [page:concepts-calendar-spread].
Holding for more than the profit target while the stock moves away [page:concepts-calendar-spread].
Illiquid underlyings: a calendar needs contracts across two expirations [page:concepts-options-liquidity].
The short calendar (sell far, buy near): its risk is larger, and after the front option expires the remaining short is effectively naked [page:concepts-calendar-spread].

setup.dte: Example: front month 30-45 DTE, back month 60-90 DTE [page:concepts-calendar-spread].
setup.strikes: At or very near the stock price to maximize exposure to IV changes; may skew slightly bullish or bearish [page:concepts-calendar-spread].
setup.credit_target: Debit trade; no debit target found beyond paying as little extrinsic as the structure requires. Sell the nearer expiration and buy the farther one for capital efficiency [page:concepts-calendar-spread].
setup.underlying: Liquid stocks and ETFs; not volatility instruments [page:concepts-calendar-spread].

manage.profit_target: About 25% of the debit paid; the page's FAQ gives a 10-25% range, saying above 25% hits less often and below 10% pays too little [page:concepts-calendar-spread]. The general rule for calendars, diagonals and iron flies is 10-50% of max profit [page:concepts-managing-winners].
manage.time_exit: No fixed time exit found. Avoid waiting for more profit, because stock movement hurts [page:concepts-calendar-spread].
manage.roll: No tastylive guidance found in the reviewed pages for rolling calendars.
manage.defend: Usually no management; same-strike spreads leave little to adjust [page:concepts-calendar-spread].
manage.loss_rule: No stop; the debit paid is the accepted max loss [page:concepts-calendar-spread].

size.bpr_formula: Defined-risk debit: net debit x 100 (the debit is the max loss); low buying-power need, lost if the short option is the longer-dated one [page:concepts-calendar-spread].
size.per_trade: Keep each trade under about 5% of the account [page:concepts-number-of-occurrences].
size.notes: Part of the 25-50% options sleeve, never above 75% [ep:options-jive-2023-12-27@06:56]. The low buying-power need makes it IRA-friendly per tastylive [page:concepts-calendar-spread]; IRAs allow defined-risk spreads [lit:tastytrade-ira-2026]. Cash accounts marked false because the short leg is covered by a different expiration (not yet verified).

evidence.note: Tastylive-only: one concept page, no episode study, no reproduction. A calendar is a theta and vega structure whose payoff depends on the stock staying near the strike and on the vol of both expiries; the trade has a stated mid-40s% success rate, below a coin flip, so its edge, if any, would come from entry pricing, which no source in the bundle tests. The literature on IV timing is indirect and does not support IV rank as a timing edge for sellers [lit:fallon-park-2016] [lit:cheng-2019]; in single names a more upward-sloping IV term structure preceded higher straddle returns for buyers [lit:vasquez-2017], but no test of calendar spreads is in the bundle.

conventions.rule: Take profit at about 25% of the debit (10-25% range)
conventions.effect: Raises the win frequency relative to waiting, keeps winners small, and frees capital sooner; because the strategy's win rate is only in the mid-40s%, this limits how often the stock drifts away before the target [page:concepts-calendar-spread] [page:concepts-managing-winners]. Adds no edge by itself [lit:williams-1991].

conventions.rule: Do not manage losers; the debit is the max loss
conventions.effect: Caps the loss at the debit and avoids chasing a moved stock; losing trades lose the debit [page:concepts-calendar-spread].

conventions.rule: Trade only in the lowest-IV environments
conventions.effect: Cheaper entry with room for IV to rise, but an indirect literature signal says IV rank is not a reliable timing signal [page:concepts-calendar-spread] [lit:fallon-park-2016].

mistakes: Holding for more than the profit target while the stock moves away from the strike [page:concepts-calendar-spread].
Trading calendars in volatility instruments [page:concepts-calendar-spread].
Reversing the legs (short calendar) without realizing the risk is much larger [page:concepts-calendar-spread].
Placing strikes far from the stock, which cuts the exposure to IV changes [page:concepts-calendar-spread].

cards.name: Diagonal spread
cards.one_liner: Buy a longer-dated in-the-money or at-the-money option and sell a nearer-dated, further out-of-the-money option of the same type: a defined-risk directional debit trade that cuts its cost by selling short-term premium against the long.

greeks.delta: + for the call version, - for the put version
greeks.theta: + (the short near-term option decays faster than the long, a temporary hedge)

when.iv: Consider long-premium structures including diagonals when IV is low and options are cheap [page:concepts-implied-volatility]; when volatility is low the hosts shift toward covered calls, ATM debit spreads, diagonals or calendars [ep:market-measures-2025-12-19@04:24]. The diagonal page itself notes profit can also come from IV rising [page:concepts-diagonal-spread].
when.outlook: Directional: bullish with the call version, bearish with the put version [page:concepts-diagonal-spread].
when.events: Earnings: sell the inflated near-term IV and hold directional delta in a back month with less exposure to the IV crush, if directionally right [page:concepts-diagonal-spread].

avoid: Volatility instruments: each expiration acts as its own underlying, so max loss is not defined [page:concepts-diagonal-spread].
A poor setup where the short premium is smaller than the long option's extrinsic value: it can lose money even if the move comes too fast [page:concepts-diagonal-spread].
Paying a debit above the spread width, which risks a loss even on a big in-the-money move [page:concepts-10-options-strategies-every-trader-should-know] [page:concepts-diagonal-spread].
Treating the short option as a permanent hedge; it is only temporary [page:concepts-diagonal-spread].
Illiquid underlyings: the trade needs contracts in two expirations [page:concepts-options-liquidity].

setup.dte: No fixed DTE found on the diagonal pages: later expiration for the long, nearer expiration for the short [page:concepts-diagonal-spread]. (The related poor man's covered call uses a short call 30-60 days out and a long call months to years out; see that card.)
setup.strikes: Long option in or at the money in the later expiration; short option out of the money in the nearer one. Check the long option's extrinsic value and sell a near-term option whose premium is at least as large; a deeper in-the-money long makes this easier [page:concepts-diagonal-spread].
setup.credit_target: Debit trade. Keep the total debit at or under 75% of the strike width, and never pay more than the width [page:concepts-diagonal-spread]. The overview page says ideally no more than 75-80% of the width [page:concepts-10-options-strategies-every-trader-should-know].
setup.underlying: Not volatility instruments [page:concepts-diagonal-spread]; liquid stocks and ETFs [page:concepts-options-liquidity].

manage.profit_target: Close at 25-50% of max profit; profit comes from the long moving further ITM and/or IV rising [page:concepts-diagonal-spread]. General guidance for calendars, diagonals and iron flies is 10-50% of max profit [page:concepts-managing-winners].
manage.time_exit: No fixed time exit found for diagonals.
manage.roll: Roll the short option down closer to breakeven when the stock moves against the spread to collect more premium; or roll the short out in time toward the long expiration, or vertically toward the long strike [page:concepts-diagonal-spread]. Roll for a credit only, as a general rule [page:concepts-defending-positions].
manage.defend: Adjust the short option when the stock moves against the spread, keeping the net debit below the spread width after moving the short strike [page:concepts-diagonal-spread].
manage.loss_rule: No stop given; the trader decides whether to close for a loss or defend the long option. Max loss is the debit paid [page:concepts-diagonal-spread].

size.bpr_formula: Defined risk: net debit x 100 (the risk equals the debit paid) [page:concepts-diagonal-spread]. Margin treatment of a diagonal with different expirations in a margin account is not yet verified.
size.per_trade: Keep each trade under about 5% of the account [page:concepts-number-of-occurrences].
size.notes: Part of the 25-50% options sleeve, never above 75% [ep:options-jive-2023-12-27@06:56]. IRAs allow defined-risk spreads [lit:tastytrade-ira-2026]; whether a given IRA tier accepts this exact diagonal was not verified. Cash accounts marked false because the short leg is covered by a different expiration (not yet verified).

cards.name: Long vertical (debit spread)
cards.one_liner: Buy one option and sell a further-out-of-the-money option of the same type and expiration for a net debit: a cheaper, defined-risk bet on a moderate move that caps both the loss and the gain.

when.iv: Low IV rank is preferred: buy verticals then, to stay engaged and as a hedge against short-volatility exposure [page:concepts-vertical-spread] [page:concepts-mean-reversion-explained]. When volatility is low the hosts shift to at-the-money debit spreads, diagonals or calendars [ep:market-measures-2025-12-19@04:24]. Rising IV helps the spread slightly, falling IV hurts [page:concepts-bull-call-spread] [page:concepts-debit-spreads].
when.outlook: Moderately bullish (call version) or moderately bearish (put version); needs a directional view [page:concepts-debit-spreads]. Poor fit when a very large move is expected, since profit is capped [page:concepts-bear-put-spread] [page:concepts-bull-call-spread].
when.events: No tastylive guidance found in the reviewed pages on events for debit spreads.

avoid: Expecting a huge move: profit is capped at the strike width minus the debit [page:concepts-bull-call-spread].
When the stock may not clear the breakeven by expiration [page:concepts-bull-call-spread].
Starting both legs OTM: cheaper, but it needs a bigger move and lowers the probability [page:concepts-vertical-debit-spread].
Closing only the short leg, which can multiply risk [page:concepts-vertical-spread].
When a comparable OTM credit spread has better liquidity and a tighter bid-ask [page:concepts-vertical-debit-spread].

setup.dte: No tastylive guidance found in the reviewed pages.
setup.strikes: Call version: buy the lower-strike (ITM) call, sell a higher-strike (ATM/OTM) call. Put version: buy the higher-strike (ITM) put, sell a lower-strike put. Make the short option carry more extrinsic value than the long so the breakeven is better than the stock price [page:concepts-vertical-debit-spread]. When buying options, use spreads rather than naked longs and aim for a breakeven at or slightly better than the current price [page:concepts-probability-of-profit].
setup.credit_target: Not applicable: this is a debit. Enter both legs as one order at the calculated net debit or within an acceptable range [page:concepts-debit-spreads] [page:concepts-volatility-skew].
setup.underlying: No tastylive guidance found on underlyings for debit spreads; liquidity matters because both legs must fill [page:concepts-options-liquidity].

manage.profit_target: Close at about 50% of max profit (example: $125 on a $250 maximum); a guideline, profits can be taken any time [page:concepts-vertical-spread].
manage.time_exit: No tastylive time exit found for debit spreads in the reviewed pages. A profitable spread can be left to expire; narrow or ATM spreads are best closed just before expiration to avoid one leg being exercised and the other expiring [page:concepts-debit-spreads] [page:concepts-options-expiration].
manage.roll: Rolling a vertical for a credit is generally difficult [page:concepts-vertical-spread].
manage.defend: Losing debit spreads are generally not defended; the maximum loss is known at entry. Adjusting on a changed view is possible but adds cost [page:concepts-vertical-spread] [page:concepts-debit-spreads].
manage.loss_rule: No stop rule; the loss is capped at the net debit paid, and the spread can be closed any time before expiration to avoid assignment or fees [page:concepts-vertical-spread]. The tastylive 2x-credit stop is for credit trades, not debit spreads [page:concepts-defending-positions].

size.bpr_formula: Net debit paid x 100 per spread; the debit is the maximum loss. (Defined-risk long premium: no margin beyond the debit is stated, though the bear put spread page notes a margin deposit may be required and can tie up capital in small accounts [page:concepts-bear-put-spread]. Broker treatment not yet verified.)
size.per_trade: Treat the debit as the risk: about 1% of the portfolio per trade, 2% in the aggressive variant [page:concepts-risk-management]; under 5% in any case [page:concepts-number-of-occurrences].
size.notes: Cash account use of spreads is not sourced (not yet verified). In IRAs, defined-risk spreads are allowed in the Basic and The Works tiers [lit:tastytrade-ira-2026]. Keep the options sleeve within 25-50% of buying power, never above 75% [ep:options-jive-2023-12-27@06:56].

conventions.effect: Caps the damage from repeated full-premium losers (lower account variance, same trade edge) [page:concepts-risk-management].

mistakes: Holding to expiration, which makes it a low-probability trade [page:concepts-strangle].
Trading it when the stock is likely to sit still [page:concepts-strangle].
Assuming low IV rank means cheap: implied volatility exceeded realized on 88% of days even at IV rank 0-20 [repro:vrp_spx].
Buying event options at wide retail spreads [lit:desilva-etal-2025].
