cards.name: Protective put / index put spread
cards.one_liner: Own the shares and buy a put on them as insurance: you pay a premium for a floor under the position, and that premium is a drag whenever the stock does not fall.

when.iv: No tastylive IV guidance found in the reviewed pages. Puts carry a volatility premium, so buying them costs more than the average realized move justifies [lit:israelov-2018] [lit:bakshi-kapadia-2003].
when.outlook: Long-term bullish on the shares but worried about a near-term drop, and unwilling to sell [page:concepts-hedging] [page:concepts-protective-put].
when.events: No tastylive guidance found in the reviewed pages on specific events. Index puts paid in fast crashes and failed in slow bears (see stats) [repro:cboe_tail_hedge].

avoid: When you are risk-tolerant and chasing returns: the premium drags performance [page:concepts-hedging].
When repeated premium would exceed the benefit if the stock does not fall [page:concepts-protective-put].
As a permanent overlay: monthly 5% OTM index puts trailed the S&P 500 total return by 2.8-3.5 points a year [repro:cboe_tail_hedge].
When the real goal is just less risk: holding less equity gave a shallower drawdown for the same return [repro:cboe_tail_hedge] [lit:israelov-2018].

setup.dte: Longer expirations give more time but cost more premium; duration is the key trade-off. No fixed DTE found in the reviewed pages [page:concepts-protective-put].
setup.strikes: The strike sets the floor price at which the shares can be sold [page:concepts-protective-put]. tastylive's example uses a $45 put on a $50 stock [page:concepts-hedging]. No delta rule found in the reviewed pages.
setup.credit_target: Debit strategy: the premium is the cost of the hedge. No target found in the reviewed pages.
setup.underlying: Shares already held or newly bought; one put covers 100 shares [page:concepts-protective-put]. For a diversified portfolio the index put or put spread version is the alias; no tastylive setup found for it in the reviewed pages.

manage.profit_target: No tastylive profit target found in the reviewed pages; the put is insurance, not a profit trade.
manage.time_exit: No fixed exit found. Do not let the put expire while you still want protection: you are unprotected if the stock then drops [page:concepts-protective-put].
manage.roll: Sell the near put and buy a later-dated one at once, or buy a new put after expiry; rolling keeps continuous protection [page:concepts-protective-put].
manage.defend: Monitor the risk and adjust or close the hedge if the risk fades [page:concepts-hedging].
manage.loss_rule: The loss is defined: the fall down to the strike plus the premium paid [page:concepts-hedging]. If the shares fall below the strike, the put can be exercised to sell at the strike [page:concepts-protective-put].

size.bpr_formula: Defined risk: the put debit paid. The stock leg is stock cost, with Reg T initial margin of 50% if bought on margin [lit:frb-regt-220-12-nd]. Portfolio margin uses stress tests [lit:tastytrade-pm-2026].
size.per_trade: One put contract covers 100 shares, so 200 shares need two puts for full protection; hedging a portion (one put) saves premium [page:concepts-protective-put]. tastylive's general rule is to risk about 1% of the portfolio per trade (up to 2% if aggressive) [page:concepts-risk-management].
size.notes: Cost versus protection is the sizing question: a smaller position (or less equity) can cut drawdown more cheaply than puts [repro:cboe_tail_hedge] [lit:israelov-2018].

cards.name: Tail hedge (far OTM puts)
cards.one_liner: Hold a small standing position in far out-of-the-money puts that pays off only in a crash; the evidence says the premium costs about 3 points of return a year, so the case rests on whether the crash protection is worth that.

when.iv: No tastylive guidance found in the reviewed pages. Long options lose on average to the volatility premium, less away from the money and more when volatility is high [lit:bakshi-kapadia-2003].
when.outlook: Defensive: protect against a sudden large drop. Puts reprice at once on a jump but did not help in the slow 2022 decline [lit:noguerialonso-alfallouji-2026] [repro:cboe_tail_hedge].
when.events: No tastylive guidance found in the reviewed pages.

avoid: As an unquestioned permanent drag: rolled index puts cost about 2.8-3.5 points of CAGR a year [repro:cboe_tail_hedge].
When the aim is only a smaller drawdown: holding less equity achieved a shallower drawdown for the same return [repro:cboe_tail_hedge] [lit:israelov-2018].
Relying on it for slow bear markets: puts failed to help in 2022 [repro:cboe_tail_hedge].
Relying on the claim that tail hedges raise long-run growth: it rests on unaudited, press-reported data from 2008-2020 [lit:universa-2020].

setup.dte: No tastylive guidance found in the reviewed pages. The tests used one-month rolls; tenor and monetization rules change results a lot [repro:cboe_tail_hedge] [lit:bhansali-etal-2020].
setup.strikes: No tastylive guidance found in the reviewed pages. The tested design was a monthly 5% OTM put (PPUT); 5-10% OTM puts were cheaper than ATM but a worse cost/benefit trade [repro:cboe_tail_hedge] [lit:harvey-etal-2019].
setup.credit_target: Debit strategy: the cost is the premium. No target found.
setup.underlying: Broad index (the studies use the S&P 500) [lit:harvey-etal-2019].

manage.profit_target: No tastylive guidance found in the reviewed pages. Proponents argue monetization rules drive value (paper not read in this review) [lit:bhansali-etal-2020].
manage.time_exit: No tastylive guidance found in the reviewed pages; the tested rule was a monthly roll [repro:cboe_tail_hedge].
manage.roll: Monthly rolling is the tested design and carries the full cost drag [repro:cboe_tail_hedge].
manage.defend: No tastylive guidance found in the reviewed pages.
manage.loss_rule: Defined risk: the premium paid.

size.bpr_formula: Defined risk: the debit paid per put; long options can be held in cash accounts and IRAs [lit:tastytrade-ira-2026].
size.per_trade: Think of it as an annual cost: a 3%/yr overlay must save about 30 points of drawdown roughly once a decade just to pay for itself (illustrative arithmetic) [lit:bondarenko-2019].
size.notes: Compare against holding less equity or adding trend following before paying the premium [repro:cboe_tail_hedge] [lit:ilmanen-etal-2021].

Buying after a spike: volatility mean-reverts [repro:vix_spikes].

cards.name: Futures options (/ES, /MES, /CL, /GC, /ZB ...)
cards.one_liner: A product, not a strategy: options whose underlying is a futures contract, giving the same structures (strangles, spreads, hedges) with larger notional, futures-style margin and 60/40 tax treatment.

when.iv: No tastylive IV guidance found in the reviewed pages for futures options as such; apply the guidance of the structure you trade.
when.outlook: Depends on the structure. To judge whether an oil shock will last, tastylive reads the futures curve: steep near-month backwardation with flat back months means the market sees it as short-lived; a lifting back end signals a longer-term problem [ep:math-check-2026-04-01@05:48].
when.events: No tastylive guidance found in the reviewed pages.

avoid: Selling futures options naked without a risk management plan: the risk is large [page:concepts-futures-options].
Illiquid futures options: hard to enter or exit at good prices, so check liquidity first [page:concepts-futures-options].
Trading a product before knowing its point value and notional [page:concepts-notional-value].
Backwardation and thin liquidity can reverse suddenly when rolling or running curve trades [page:concepts-backwardation].
Taking undefined risk in an IRA: naked puts are not allowed, and futures need the top IRA tier [lit:tastytrade-ira-2026].
